aiExplanation: This function finds the **maximum distance** between elements of two arrays by checking all pairs where an element from **`nums1`** at index `i` is less than or equal to an element from **`nums2`** at index `j` (where `j >= i`). It uses nested loops: for each element in `nums1`, it searches through `nums2` starting from the same index, and whenever it finds an element in `nums2` that is at least as large, it calculates the distance as `j - i`; if it encounters a smaller element in `nums2`, it stops searching for that position in `nums1` (since `nums2` would only get smaller). The function tracks the largest distance found across all valid pairs and **returns** that maximum value, or **0** if no valid pair exists.

author: Vitor
aiExplanation: This code finds the **maximum distance between indices** in two arrays using a **two-pointer technique**. It maintains two pointers (`pos1` and `pos2`) that iterate through `nums1` and `nums2` respectively. When `nums1[pos1] > nums2[pos2]`, the current elements can't be validly paired, so it advances `pos1` forward (and syncs `pos2` to maintain proper indexing). Otherwise, when `nums1[pos1] <= nums2[pos2]`, the elements form a valid pair, and the code calculates the distance (`pos2 - pos1`) and tracks the maximum. The algorithm continues advancing `pos2` to explore other potential pairs, ultimately returning the largest distance found between any two valid index pairs where the value constraint is satisfied.
